chunks: Al-Hasan al-Sayqal narrated from Abu Ubaydah al-Hadhdha', who said:

Abu Ja'far عليه السلام said: "Samurah ibn Jundub had a date-palm tree in the garden of a certain family. Whenever he came to his tree, he would look at something of the man's household that the man disliked."

He said: "So the man went to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and complained about him. He said: O Messenger of Allah, Samurah enters upon me without my permission, so if you would send to him and order him to seek permission, so that my family may take precautions against him. So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم sent for him and called him, and said: O Samurah, what is the matter with so-and-so complaining of you and saying that you enter without my permission and then see of his family what he dislikes? O Samurah, seek permission when you enter."

Then the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: "Would it please you to have a cluster in Paradise in exchange for your palm tree?" He said: No. He said: "You shall have three." He said: No. He said: "I see you, O Samurah, as nothing but one who causes harm. Go, O so-and-so, cut it down and strike his face with it."

key_terms.عَذْقٌ: a date-palm cluster or branch, here promised in Paradise
key_terms.مُضَارًّا: someone causing harm or injury to others
key_terms.نَخْلَةٌ: a date-palm tree owned by Samurah within another man's garden

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith of Samurah ibn Jundub teach about causing harm and entering property without permission?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts the case of Samurah ibn Jundub, whose access to his palm tree caused harm and violated the privacy of another household. The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم instructed him to seek permission, then offered him compensation, and when he refused, ordered the tree removed because of the harm he was causing.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3423 - Al-Hasan al-Sayqal narrated from Abu Ubaydah al-Hadhdha', who said that

Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) said:
"Samurah ibn Jundub had a date palm tree in the orchard of a certain man. Whenever he came to his tree, he would see things related to the man's family that the man disliked being seen.

The man went to the Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace be upon him and his family) and complained about him, saying: O Messenger of Allah (swt), Samurah enters my property without my permission. Would you send for him and command him to seek permission, so that my family can take precautions against him?' The Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace be upon him and his family) sent for Samurah and said to him: O Samurah, what is this matter that so-and-so complains about you, saying that you enter his property without permission and see things from his family that he dislikes? O Samurah, seek permission when you enter.'

Then the Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Would it please you (Samurah) to have a date palm branch in Paradise in exchange for your tree?' He (Samurah) replied: 'No.' The Prophet said: 'You will have three (branches in Paradise).' He (Samurah) again said: 'No.' The Prophet then said: 'I do not see you, O Samurah, except as someone who causes harm. O so-and-so, cut down his tree and throw it in his face.'"
